correlations.question: Does the closing spread predict the final home margin?
correlations.inputs: officially sourced / labelled third-party archive; see source column
correlations.note: the market's own coherence check; r near 0 would mean the archive's sign is wrong

correlations.question: Does the closing total predict the actual combined score?
correlations.inputs: officially sourced / labelled third-party archive; see source column
correlations.note: 136 games; the total is harder to price than the side and this quantifies that
correlations.caveat: a low r here is expected and is not an error

correlations.question: Is our fair spread a repackaging of the market number?
correlations.inputs: officially sourced / labelled third-party archive; see source column
correlations.note: the single most important anti-fraud check on this site: if r were ~1.0 our 'own' line would be a copy, not an origination
correlations.caveat: computed after the walk-forward model saw only prior weeks

correlations.question: Does rest differential correlate with home margin?
correlations.inputs: officially sourced / labelled third-party archive; see source column
correlations.note: rest is derived arithmetically from the archived official gamedates, so both inputs are traceable
correlations.robustness_note: x is a GROUP VARIABLE, not a continuous one: 62% of the n=120 observations share the single value 0. The Pearson r is dominated by the small tail groups listed alongside it. Read the group means and their n, not the r.
correlations.caveat: n is smaller than 136 because week-1 clubs have no prior game

correlations.question: Across clubs, are points scored and points conceded correlated?
correlations.inputs: officially sourced / labelled third-party archive; see source column
correlations.note: 32 clubs; a near-zero r supports modelling offence and defence separately, a strong negative r would support a single strength axis
correlations.caveat: club-level n=32, so the interval is wide by construction

correlations.question: Does injury designation predict snap share?
correlations.note: requires a per-player snap-count feed joined to designations. The official injury page read this session carries no snap counts and the repository holds no snap-count archive.

correlations.question: Does a backup replacing a starter cost points?
correlations.note: requires (a) a confirmed inactive list and (b) a depth rank per club. The official injury table has no depth column and 6 of its rows carry a game designation.
correlations.blocked_by: no inactive list + no depth rank

correlations.question: Are same-game parlay legs dependent?
correlations.note: player-level outcomes are not in the vendored archive, and no price source exists for legs. Publishing a dependence estimate here would be fabrication.
correlations.blocked_by: no player-level official feed, no leg prices

warnings: n=136 is one season. A correlation that survives one season has not been shown to survive another.
CR-03 is a fraud check, not a performance claim.
Multiple comparisons: 5 computed values at alpha=0.05 implies ~0.25 false positives by chance. Treat any single p as descriptive.
